requirements.title: SandboxDriver Interface Definition
requirements.description: Define a SandboxDriver interface with pluggable implementations. First-class Linux overlayfs driver, with an explicit tracking-only copy contract for non-Linux environments and no hardcoded Linux assumptions in APIs.

validation.notes: Driver interface exists with all required methods (Type, Version, IsAvailable, Mount, etc.)
DriverType enum includes overlayfs, copy, and none types
Authoritative storage paths ignore desktop-session and application-level directory variables.
An unusable authoritative directory fails closed without selecting an alternate path.
Protected containment requests fail closed when the platform backend is unavailable.
Real-Apple-hardware driver selection and Seatbelt evidence are required before this cross-platform contract can be complete.

requirements.title: CopyDriver Implementation
requirements.description: Cross-platform CopyDriver that works on any OS using file copies instead of overlayfs. Copies scope directory to create snapshot, compares workspace against original for diff generation. Higher disk usage but universal compatibility.

validation.notes: CopyDriver.IsAvailable returns true on any platform
CopyDriver correctly creates workspace via Mount
CopyDriver correctly detects added, modified, deleted files
CopyDriver mount state tracking works correctly
CopyDriver file removal with path traversal protection
CopyDriver Unmount is a safe no-op
The copy driver is build-verified; its macOS behavior remains pending the documented Apple-hardware shakeout.

requirements.title: Automatic Driver Selection
requirements.description: SelectDriver function automatically chooses the best available driver. Prefers overlayfs on Linux, falls back to CopyDriver on other platforms. DriverInfo provides information about available drivers.

validation.notes: SelectDriver falls back to CopyDriver when overlayfs unavailable
DriverInfo returns info about all available drivers
Darwin cross-builds and unit tests are insufficient to claim real-host selection behavior.
